standfirst: One genus, one genome layout: a ~241 kDa ORF1 polyprotein carrying the coat protein at its C-terminus, and a 36 kDa ORF2 movement protein. Three features, built from 779 unique proteins, routing 100% of the taxon on 13 references.

modules.Capillovirus: Small and homogeneous, so the work was in the annotation strings rather than the biology. Three different labels -- serine protease, 36K protein and putative movement protein -- turned out to be 96.9-98.4% identical to one another and are all ORF2; the protease label is simply wrong, since capilloviruses encode a papain-like cysteine protease as an ORF1 domain.

gaps: The only strings not modelled are ORF1 domain footprints -- 26 features annotated RNA-dependent RNA polymerase core region, every one of them exactly 270 aa, which is a Pfam hit rather than a separate CDS. Declaring it would create a feature no genome separately encodes.
derived: No cleaved products are declared. ORF1 is a polyprotein and its mature peptides have no coordinates in the literature that could be read off the sequence, so none are claimed.

why.CP: 45 sequences after 11 records whose CP is annotated inside the ORF1 polyprotein were dropped on the Met rule -- 8 of them beginning at Ile at exactly 205 aa. Built at -m 2.
